# Festivalleitung

## Working unit

One festival Ruben directs, or one edition of it. He is neither engaged nor a
guest: the appointment is the arrangement, and it covers work he conducts
himself as well as productions he does not conduct but is answerable for.

The working unit is the project as the notebook records it, usually gathered on
a `CL` page — `CL Aufgaben`, but also `CL Status & Termine`, `CL Konditionen`,
`CL Abrechnungsoptionen` and others; the notebooks name them differently.
A project without one may still be a full working unit;
what decides is whether the section records enough to work from. Where it
records almost nothing, say the project is too thin to classify and ask.

## Classifying a project into this category

From what the pages record. The marks of Festivalleitung:

- An appointment or an agreement to direct, rather than a contract for a
  performance. Whether he will direct it at all can itself be undecided, and
  waiting on a meeting or a decision between candidates is a legitimate state
  for a project to be in — report the decision as the open item.
- Responsibility spanning more than the concert he conducts.
- A festival office of his own to delegate to — musician management,
  accommodation — where a BCW project would use the ensemble office.

A festival appearing in a project title does not make the project
Festivalleitung. Being engaged to play at somebody else's festival is a BCW
engagement or a Gastdirigat.

This is the category with the least recorded evidence in the surveyed notebook:
one festival with live work, one whose appointment has just been confirmed and
whose planning has not begun. Treat this playbook as the thinnest of the four
and say so where it matters.

## Expected evidence

Festival dates and whether they are confirmed, the appointment and the years it
covers, the concert or concerts he conducts himself, other productions in the
programme and what he owes them, the musician list and who manages it,
accommodation and who arranges it, repertoire and Noten, and the people at the
festival who hold each of these.

## The shape

Where he conducts, the work follows the BCW pattern — programme, musicians,
Noten einrichten, repertoire preparation — with the festival office in place of
the ensemble office. Where he does not conduct, his work is oversight rather
than production: something to record and ask about, not something to plan on his
behalf.

Delegation is the recurring structure. A list he finishes is handed to someone
who does the engaging; a contact on the ground is reached through that person
rather than directly. Where the page says a step is somebody else's, it is not
his open task — but "handed over" and "done" are different facts, and only the
first one is usually written down.

## Format

**Konzert.** Orchesterproben → Hauptprobe → Generalprobe, often compressed:
a rehearsal the day before and a Generalprobe on the day. Programming a festival
concert includes what a house programme does not — Zwischenstücke to rest a
singer, a Zugabe, and the balance against the rest of the festival programme.

**Mischform.** A programme combining forces or repertoire, or a concert
reshaped from a touring programme. Musical rehearsals with the soloist or
singer; orchestral rehearsals less differentiated; Hauptprobe; Generalprobe.

**Oper.** No festival opera is recorded in the surveyed notebook. If one arises,
read the rehearsal structure from "Projekt-Etappen Übersicht" rather than
assuming.

## Workflow

1. Establish which edition and which of its productions the page is about, and
   keep his own concert separate from the productions he only oversees.
2. Verify the festival dates and whether they are confirmed.
3. Identify the first commitment whose prerequisites appear met, preferring one
   that unblocks someone else — a list that another person is waiting on holds
   up more than his own preparation does.
4. Recommend one next action.
5. If outreach is useful, Registrar extracts the contact, Envoy drafts, and
   Auditor verifies before the result is shown.

## Checks

- A festival under negotiation and a festival under his direction are different
  states, and an appointment confirms the second only from the date it is
  recorded.
- A period recorded without a confirmation status is not a fixed period. A
  page title carrying dates but no year does not supply one.
- A cancelled soloist is a live problem with a replacement and a deadline
  attached to it.
- Noten einrichten is a chain with several hands in it. Which step is done is
  recorded per step, never inferred from the next one.
- Productions he does not conduct still carry obligations he holds. Where the
  page names none, they are unrecorded, not absent.
- Never infer that a delegated step was carried out because it was delegated.

## Not this playbook

Playing or conducting at a festival somebody else directs is
`project-type:bcw` when the Bach Consort Wien is engaged, and
`project-type:gastdirigat` when he conducts another orchestra.
